LESSON: READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE READING- COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can we tell the meaning of words and phrases in a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the main ideas in a text
2. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text
3. describe characters, ideas, or events in a text

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Connected text means sentences and short passages — not only single words.

• First look at any new words. Then read the whole sentence.

• If you do not understand, read again more slowly and ask: Who? What? Where?

• Fluency grows when you re-read the same short passage until it sounds smooth.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about a child walking to school in Kenya. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 2: Time yourself reading a short passage. Read it again and try to sound clearer, not only faster.

Example 3: After reading, answer: Who was in the story? What happened first?

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read a short passage aloud to a partner. Ask them to tell you one clear sentence they heard.
2. Re-read the same passage silently, then aloud once more.
3. Write two questions about the passage and swap with a friend.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Read one short story or paragraph at home and retell it in four sentences.
2. List three new words from your reading and use each in a sentence.
3. Explain to a parent what the passage was mainly about.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Download and share texts with mental images from the texts and draw conclusions,
2. Read a passage individually, and identify keywords in the passage,
3. Infer the meaning of words using contextual clues,
4. Role-play the characters and events in the text,
5. Critical thinking: It is enhanced as the learner solves simple problems as they answer questions based on the passage and give an appropriate title to the passage.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Read words in sentences, not only alone.
2. Re-reading builds fluency and confidence.
3. Always check that you understand who, what, and where.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
